description: BIP-39 mnemonic-to-seed derivation (Seed = PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512(password = sentence, salt = "mnemonic" || passphrase, iterations = 2048, dkLen = 64)), for the same four English 24-word/256-bit-entropy mnemonics bip39.v1.json validates. Each vector carries two seed values with different provenance, both under the SAME mnemonic: trezorPassphraseSeedHex is an **external** value, reproduced verbatim from the widely used Trezor python-mnemonic reference vectors (https://github.com/trezor/python-mnemonic/blob/master/vectors.json, "english" list, fixed passphrase "TREZOR") -- deriveSeed's own test uses it to pin this package's PBKDF2 wiring against a genuinely published value. emptyPassphraseSeedHex is **project-derived, not independently published**: it was computed by this repository by running the identical PBKDF2 formula with passphrase = "" instead of "TREZOR" (both a reference Python hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac computation and Go's crypto/pbkdf2, which agreed exactly), then cross-checked for internal consistency by confirming the same code path reproduces trezorPassphraseSeedHex exactly when passphrase = "TREZOR" is substituted back in -- i.e. the empty-passphrase values are trusted because the algorithm that produced them is proven correct against the external vector on the same mnemonic, not because emptyPassphraseSeedHex itself comes from an external source. Mnemonic.Seed (this package's only public seed-derivation entry point) always uses the empty passphrase, so emptyPassphraseSeedHex is what TestVectorsSeed pins Mnemonic.Seed against; trezorPassphraseSeedHex is exercised only by deriveSeed's own internal (non-exported-API) test.
